chunks: Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah, from me, and from your daughter who has come to you and hastened to meet you!

My patience regarding your chosen one has been exhausted, O Messenger of Allah, and my endurance has weakened, except that I have a place for consolation in taking comfort by the great hardship and heart-rending event of your separation.
Indeed, I laid you down in the hollow of your grave, and your soul passed between my neck and chest.
Verily we are Allah’s and verily unto Him shall we return.

key_terms.وَسَّدْتُكَ: I laid you down (with your head on my lap/chest)

ai.seo_question: What did Fatimah say about her father's death and burial?
ai.summary: This supplication, often cited in Shia tradition as spoken by Fatimah al-Zahra (peace be upon her) at the Prophet's burial, poetically captures the unique intensity of her grief as the daughter of the Messenger. It highlights the paradox of her endurance, where her patience waned due to the overwhelming intimacy of the loss, yet found solace in emulating the Prophet’s own patience during his great trial. The text underscores the profound emotional bond between the Prophet and his daughter, framing her mourning as both a personal sorrow and a spiritual lesson in steadfastness.

en.sayed-ali-raza: O Prophet of Allāh, peace be upon you from me and from your daughter who has come to you and who has hastened to meet you.

O Prophet of Allāh, my patience about your chosen (daughter) has been exhausted, and my power of endurance has weakened, except that I have ground for consolation in having endured the great hardship and heart-rending event of your separation.
I laid you down in your grave when your last breath had passed (when your head was) between my neck and chest.
... Verily we are Allāh’s and verily unto Him shall we return. (Qur’ān, 2:156)
